title: Optimal concentration in the Paley-Wiener space
summary: Let $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}$ be a bounded interval and let $PW(Ω)$ be the corresponding Paley--Wiener space. For a measurable set $E\subset \mathbb{R}$ of finite measure, consider the largest possible fraction of the $L^{2}$-mass of a function in $PW(Ω)$ that can lie in $E$. We prove that this concentration is no larger than the concentration attained on an interval of measure $\lvert E\rvert $.
